text:
julia: Hey team — PR #9124 is ready for review but it's gated on architecture sign-off. I linked the draft RFC (still a draft): https://internal.redwood/rfcs/drafts/serve-routing-v2. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9124 :wave:

matt_arch: I'll take a look later today. quick Q — does this change routing policy semantics or just add a config flag that teams opt into?

julia: It adds a new `fallback_policy` enum and wires a warm-fallback path. No behavioral changes unless customers enable the flag/rollout. I put a short summary at the top of the PR description and a tiny sequence diagram.

anya: Can you add a brief canary plan to the PR? e.g., 5% traffic for 2 hours, abort if error rate > 0.5% or p99 latency regression > 15%. That'll make architecture sign-off faster. :eyes:

julia: Yep, good call — will add canary steps and the exact perf numbers. Local perf: p50 ~12ms (no change), p99 ~78ms -> ~81ms with fallback enabled (+3ms). I'll paste the raw numbers in the PR.

sam: Ping @matt_arch — we need arch ack to keep the release train on schedule (planning to cut tomorrow).

matt_arch: Skimmed it — overall looks fine. Please do two things before I post formal LGTM: 1) add the RFC link into the PR body as "Design RFC: serve-routing-v2 (draft)" so auditing finds it, and 2) include the canary window and abort criteria in the rollout section. After that I'll give an official ack.

deploy-bot: merge-check: merging without architecture ack will fail the CI gating check `rfc-linked`.

julia: Thanks — updating PR now. Marking this thread blocked until I push the canary + RFC link. Will @mention again when done. :white_check_mark:
